title: What is a constitution?
bodyMd:
## The ground rules of the country

A constitution is the set of ground rules for how a country is governed. It says what the government may do, how power is shared, and which rights every person holds.

## Why Nigeria's Constitution matters to you

Nigeria's 1999 Constitution (as amended) is the highest law in the country. Any other law that contradicts it does not stand. That is why knowing even a little of it protects you.

## The parts you will meet most

- **Fundamental rights (Chapter IV, Sections 33–46):** life, dignity, personal liberty, fair hearing, privacy, expression, assembly, movement, freedom from discrimination, property, and how to enforce these rights.
- **Duties (Section 24):** what the Constitution asks of citizens in return.
- **Government:** how the executive, legislature and courts share power, and how federal and state powers divide.

## Rights are strong but not unlimited

Most rights have qualifications written into the Constitution itself. Whenever Citizens Lens explains a right, it also shows the exceptions — read them before acting.

## Next steps

- Read a short answer: start with everyday questions on the Home page.
- Always check the original provision quoted under each explanation.

title: You're arrested. What are your rights?
bodyMd:
## The scenario

Police stop you and say you are under arrest. You are confused and frightened. What does the Constitution say must happen?

## Step 1: You must be told why

The police must tell you the reason for the arrest. This flows from your right to personal liberty. An arrest without any stated reason is a red flag.

## Step 2: You must be treated with dignity

While detained, you have the right to dignity — no torture, beating, or degrading treatment. This applies in every police station and cell.

## Step 3: You must see a court within a reasonable time

Detention is not meant to be open-ended. You must be brought before a court within a reasonable time so a judge can review your case.

## Step 4: If your rights were violated, courts can help

Anyone who says a fundamental right was violated may apply to a High Court for redress. Note deadlines and procedures matter — get advice early, for example from a legal-aid organisation.

## What this lesson does not do

This is constitutional information, not legal advice for your situation. Criminal procedure details sit in other laws. Stay calm, note names, times and places, and contact a lawyer as soon as you can.
